paper_sections.title: Estimating effective connectivity in Alzheimer's disease progression: A dynamic causal modeling study

description.value: The study estimated resting-state effective connectivity among default mode, salience, and central executive network regions across cognitively normal, early MCI, late MCI, and Alzheimer's disease groups, and tested whether connectivity predicted MMSE and CDR scores.

design.value: A retrospective longitudinal ADNI-2 resting-state fMRI study comparing four stable progression-stage groups using dynamic causal modeling, parametric empirical Bayes, Bayesian model reduction, ANOVA, and linear regression.

description.value: Cognitive scores used for subject inclusion and as an outcome in linear regression.
Clinical dementia rating used for subject inclusion and as an outcome in linear regression.
MMSE scores above 24, CDR = 0, free of memory complaints.
MMSE scores above 24, CDR = 0.5, have subjective memory complaints, abnormal memory functions.
MMSE scores above 24, CDR = 0.5, have subjective memory complaints, abnormal memory functions (more severe compared to EMCIs).
MMSE scores ranging from 20 to 26, CDR above 0.5, have subjective memory complaints, abnormal memory functions (same as LMCIs).

task_description.value: During the fMRI scans, all participants were instructed to keep their eyes open and relax.

instructions.value: Keep their eyes open and relax.

description.value: Resting-state functional images were obtained using an echo-planar imaging sequence (EPI). Each series has 140 volumes, and each volume consists of 48 slices of image matrices with dimensions 64 × 64.

The first 10 volumes of each functional time series were discarded. The remaining 130 volumes were corrected for the staggered order of slice acquisition. Preprocessing also included regression of head motion parameters, realignment for head movement, and spatial normalization using T1 image unified segmentation to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) space.

steps.value: Spatial normalization using T1 image unified segmentation to MNI space

model_settings.value: The neuronal model included intrinsic connectivity, extrinsic connectivity, and input parameters; the resting-state stimulus was usually set to zero. The observation model was a generalized BOLD signal model. Regions of interest were modeled as nodes, with time series extracted from all voxels within an 8-mm-radius sphere around associated MNI coordinates.

estimator.value: Bayesian Model Reduction (BMR) and parametric empirical Bayes (PEB)

model_settings.value: The connectivity strengths for each subject group were compared using analysis of variance (ANOVA). Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons.
Forward step-wise linear regression was used for MMSE; both forward and backward connections between L-dlPFC and mPFC were predictive of CDR.

estimator.value: forward step-wise linear regression; forward and backward regression

description.value: Participants kept their eyes open and relaxed during the fMRI scans; stimulus u was usually set to zero in resting state models.

definition.value: The forward step-wise linear regression tested whether resting-state connectivity predicted MMSE scores. EC between left dlPFC and left PCC was the first variable entered, followed by L-dlPFC to mPFC and L-PCC to R-ACC; together they explained 11.5% of the variance in MMSE scores (R² = 0.115, F = 5.434, p = 0.002).

inference_target.value: whether EC between regions could predict subjects' cognitive scores

structured_details.value: Predictors: L-dlPFC to L-PCC (β = −0.234, p = 0.007), L-dlPFC to mPFC (β = 0.222, p = 0.01), and L-PCC to R-ACC (β = 0.168, p = 0.048); R² = 0.115; F = 5.434; p = 0.002.

reason_first_class_type_not_used.value: The analysis is a linear regression predicting a cognitive assessment from DCM-derived connectivity rather than one of the named connectivity-estimation methods.
